entries.clue: (&17/6) Having a joint after peculiar, coy sex, enjoyed less by Obama and Cameron? (7)

annotation.definition: enjoyed less by Obama and Cameron?
annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a descriptive phrase rather than a noun; it points at the thing the two leaders were enjoying less, which is a noun.

indicatorNotes.after: 'After' puts the joint behind everything that came before it, so it goes at the end.

blocks.note: Peculiar in the sense of particular to one thing is SPECIAL.
'Relations' is the coy, euphemistic word for sex.
The hip is a joint of the body.

annotation.surface: Two world leaders get a nudge about their youthful joint-smoking and a sex life that has gone off the boil.
annotation.walkthrough: The joint is a hip, not the sort Obama and Cameron were quizzed about. In 2013 news that the US had spied on its allies soured the transatlantic friendship.
annotation.definitionFit: The special relationship is the stock name for the close US-UK alliance, and the 2013 spying revelations strained it between Obama and Cameron.

entries.clue: Knicker accessories they put on ice? (10)

blocks.note: Lingerie items worn with knickers, holding up stockings.
Putting something on ice means postponing it, so this reads as people who postpone.

annotation.surface: A saucy question about what goes with knickers, with a hint of chilled lingerie.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On ice' has nothing to do with cold: it means postponed. Anyone who suspends a plan puts it on ice.
annotation.definitionFit: Suspenders are the straps that hold up stockings, part of a lingerie set, and people who suspend things put them on hold.

entries.clue: Instrument of torture's opening beneath bottle (6)

indicatorNotes.opening: The opening of a word is its first letter.
indicatorNotes.beneath: In a down entry, a piece placed beneath another comes after it.

blocks.note: Bottle is British slang for courage, and so is spine.
The first letter of 'torture'.

annotation.surface: A grim question about which instrument the torturer reaches for first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Instrument of torture' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Instrument'. Bottle means nerve in British slang, as in 'lose your bottle'.
annotation.definitionFit: A spinet is a small harpsichord-like keyboard instrument.

entries.clue: Crafty Hirst's Heart Embedded In Creative Fault (6)

indicatorNotes.Heart: The heart of a word is its middle letter.
indicatorNotes.Embedded In: Something embedded in another is set inside it.
indicatorNotes.Creative: Creative work makes something new, so the letters are rearranged.

blocks.note: The letters of 'fault' rearranged, to be split around the other piece.
The middle letter of 'Hirst'.

annotation.surface: A jibe that Damien Hirst's heart lies in a crafty, flawed kind of creativity.
annotation.walkthrough: Damien Hirst is the British artist famous for pickled sharks, so 'Crafty' and 'Creative' look like art criticism. The capitals are decoration and change nothing.
annotation.definitionFit: Artful means cunning or crafty, as with the Artful Dodger in Oliver Twist.

entries.clue: Busy getting leg over (2,3,3)

blocks.note: Busy means occupied at work.
'Getting your leg over' is British slang for having sex.

annotation.surface: Someone is too busy with other things to be interrupted.
annotation.walkthrough: Both halves are slang. 'Getting your leg over' is a British euphemism for sex, and 'on the job' covers work and sex alike.
annotation.definitionFit: On the job means at work, so busy, and it is also British slang for in the act of sex.

entries.clue: see 1dn. (4)
Putting knob in plain stocking tops gives a rounder, fatter look (6)

indicatorNotes.in: Putting one thing in another places it inside.
indicatorNotes.tops: The top of a word is its first letter.

blocks.note: The top letter of 'plain'.
A knob is a small lump.
The top letter of 'stocking'.

annotation.surface: Advice on padding plain stockings for a curvier silhouette, with a double entendre on 'knob'.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plain stocking tops' look like hosiery, but 'tops' asks for the first letter of each word. The knob sits between them.
annotation.definitionFit: To plump something, like a cushion or a pillow, is to make it rounder and fuller.

entries.clue: Digger's rather large board? (8)

blocks.note: A digger of trenches, man or machine.
A large wooden platter on which food was once served.

annotation.surface: A question about the size of a board belonging to the Digger, Private Eye's nickname for Rupert Murdoch.
annotation.walkthrough: The Digger is Private Eye's name for the Australian Rupert Murdoch, so 'board' looks like his company's boardroom. It is a board for food, and the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: The word covers both a machine that digs trenches and an old wooden serving board, which gives us 'trencherman' for a hearty eater.

entries.clue: Ringo forced to accept Beatle's final division (6)

indicatorNotes.forced: Something forced has been pushed out of its natural shape, so the letters are rearranged.
indicatorNotes.to accept: To accept something is to take it in, so the extra letter joins the mix.
indicatorNotes.final: The final part of a word is its last letter.

blocks.note: Taken as written.
The last letter of 'Beatle'.

annotation.surface: Ringo Starr grudgingly accepts the Beatles' final split.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is the Beatles breaking up. 'Final division' reads as the split, but 'final' takes the last letter of 'Beatle' and the definition is just 'division'.
annotation.definitionFit: Countries are divided into administrative areas, and each such area is called a region.

entries.clue: Scratchy firm buttocks (6)

blocks.note: CO is short for company, a firm.
Arse is British slang for buttocks.

annotation.surface: A cheeky comment on a bottom that is firm but rough to the touch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Firm buttocks' reads as a compliment. The firm is a company, CO, and the buttocks are spelt the British way.
annotation.definitionFit: Coarse fabric is rough in texture, so it is scratchy against the skin.

entries.clue: Having covered head fattened cock (5)

blocks.note: Having your head covered means wearing a hat, two words that run together.
A cockerel castrated and fattened for the table.

annotation.surface: A rude image of a well-fed member with something over its tip.
annotation.walkthrough: The second reading is two words, CAP ON, which run together into the bird.
annotation.definitionFit: A capon is a cockerel castrated and fattened for eating, and anyone with a cap on has a covered head.

entries.clue: Ready-made toff screwed diplomat Margaret (3,3,3)

indicatorNotes.screwed: Something screwed up is twisted out of shape, so its letters are rearranged.

blocks.note: The letters of 'toff' rearranged.
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador.
Peg is a pet form of Margaret.

annotation.surface: Gossip about an upper-class man who seduced a female diplomat called Margaret.
annotation.walkthrough: The toff and 'screwed' are a Private Eye tabloid scandal, but only the toff's letters get screwed. The diplomat is HE, His Excellency.
annotation.definitionFit: Off-the-peg clothes are bought ready-made from the rail rather than tailored.

entries.clue: Archer's chief untrue representation about a large nude (2,7)

indicatorNotes.chief: The chief part of a word is its head, the first letter.
indicatorNotes.representation: A representation is a new version of something, so the letters are rearranged.
indicatorNotes.about: About means around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece.

blocks.note: The first letter of 'Archer'.
The letters of 'untrue' rearranged, to be split around the next piece.
Taken as written.
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large.

annotation.surface: A dig at Jeffrey Archer, the Tory novelist jailed for perjury, telling lies about a large nude.
annotation.walkthrough: The Archer is Jeffrey Archer, jailed for perjury, so 'untrue representation' suits him. The anagram of 'untrue' opens around the lone 'a'.
annotation.definitionFit: Au naturel is French for 'in the natural state', used in English to mean naked.

entries.clue: Bum around, protected by girl of very large size (5)

indicatorNotes.around: Shoved around, the letters end up in a different order.
indicatorNotes.protected by: Something protected by another sits inside it, as if sheltered.

blocks.note: Jo is a girl's name.
The letters of 'bum' rearranged, to sit inside the girl.

annotation.surface: A girl shields a large-bottomed loafer, or else it is a crack about her own size.
annotation.walkthrough: Crossword girls are short names like JO, ANN or UNA. 'Bum around' sounds like loafing, but it asks for the letters of 'bum' to be shuffled.
annotation.definitionFit: Jumbo, from the name of a famous elephant, means extra large, as in a jumbo jet.

entries.clue: Candidate with rubbish policy no good in misruled cock-up? (10)

indicatorNotes.in: In puts the no-good letters among the other letters.
indicatorNotes.cock-up: A cock-up is a botch, so the letters come out jumbled.

blocks.note: NG is the abbreviation for no good.
Taken as written.

annotation.surface: An election candidate with a useless manifesto botches the job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish policy' reads as a poor manifesto. It is a policy of throwing dirt, not a bad one.
annotation.definitionFit: A mudslinger is a campaigner whose policy is to smear opponents, throwing verbal rubbish at them.

entries.clue: Miliband U-turn on original American statute (6)

indicatorNotes.U-turn: A U-turn makes something go back the way it came, so the letters read backwards.

blocks.note: Ed Miliband gives ED, which the U-turn turns into DE.
The Cree are a First Nations people, original inhabitants of North America.

annotation.surface: Labour leader Ed Miliband performs a U-turn over a piece of historic American legislation.
annotation.walkthrough: Ed Miliband was Labour leader in 2013, and his first name gives ED. 'Original American' points to a Native American people rather than to the Constitution.
annotation.definitionFit: A decree is an official order with the force of law, so a statute in the loose sense.

entries.clue: see 1dn. (8)
Hardly a celeb wanting just head (6)

blocks.note: Hardly a celeb means a person of no importance at all.
Wanting all but the head means lacking the rest of the body, two words that run together.

annotation.surface: A smutty line about someone who, far from famous, is interested only in oral sex.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head' tempts a rude reading. Here it means a head with no body attached, and those two words run together.
annotation.definitionFit: A nobody is an unimportant person, hardly a celebrity, and a head alone has no body.

entries.clue: Its count got high, as far as some tabloids were concerned (6)

annotation.definition: Its count got high, as far as some tabloids were concerned

blocks.note: The surface suggests a statistic that climbed, or a nobleman on drugs.

blocks.clueFragment: as far as some tabloids were concerned
blocks.note: The setter means the Sun's Page 3 topless models, so the thing being tallied is a part of the bare breast.

annotation.surface: A tabloid story about a count getting stoned.
annotation.walkthrough: Private Eye mocked the Sun's Page 3 topless models throughout 2013, when a campaign to scrap them was in the news. The count is a tally, not a nobleman.
annotation.definitionFit: Tabloid Page 3 pictures meant a high tally of this body part, shown on every topless model.

entries.clue: Virgin lunatic due to take over tabloid (6)

indicatorNotes.lunatic: Something lunatic has gone mad, so the letters are scrambled.
indicatorNotes.take: To take something is to take it in, so the scrambled letters hold the tabloid.
indicatorNotes.over: Turned over, a word reads the other way round.

blocks.note: The letters of 'due' rearranged, to be split around the tabloid.
The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, and turned over it gives NUS.

annotation.surface: Richard Branson's Virgin is set to buy a tabloid newspaper, a mad scheme.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Virgin' looks like Branson's company, but it means untouched. 'Take over' sounds like a business deal and does two jobs: take in, and turn over.
annotation.definitionFit: Unused means never used, as virgin snow or a virgin page is untouched.

entries.clue: The bastard in long hair's 'a real gas' (7)

indicatorNotes.bastard: A bastard form is a corrupted one, so the letters of 'the' are rearranged.
indicatorNotes.in: In puts one piece inside the other.

blocks.note: A mane is a long head of hair, split around the other piece.
The letters of 'the' rearranged.

annotation.surface: A long-haired rotter is called 'a real gas', slang for great fun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A real gas' is old slang for a lot of fun, which suits a rogue with flowing hair. Taken literally, it is exactly what methane is.
annotation.definitionFit: Methane is a real, literal gas, the main part of natural gas.

entries.clue: Agency that has sent up people – length of a certain body part (5)

blocks.clueFragment: Agency that has sent up people
blocks.note: NASA is the US space agency, which has sent astronauts up.
L is the abbreviation for length.

annotation.surface: A coy remark about the length of a certain body part, the kind the Eye enjoys.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A certain body part' hints at something ruder. The body part is the nose.
annotation.definitionFit: Nasal means of or relating to the nose.

entries.clue: Pursue ... leg over – a real sticker (9)

indicatorNotes.over: Something knocked over is upset, so the letters are rearranged.

blocks.note: Taken as written.
Taken as written.

annotation.surface: Someone chases a leg-over, and sticks at it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leg over' recalls 5 down's slang for sex, but here the leg goes into the mix. The ellipsis just stitches the surface together.
annotation.definitionFit: Superglue is a strong instant adhesive, so it truly sticks.

entries.clue: Wedging tool between two poles, spurts out eggs (6)

indicatorNotes.Wedging: Wedging something forces it into a gap, so it sits inside.
indicatorNotes.between: Between places the piece with one thing on each side of it.

blocks.note: S for south pole, the first of the two.
A pawn is someone used as a tool by others.
The second pole is also S.

annotation.surface: A wedge is forced between two poles, and something spurts out.
annotation.walkthrough: The tool is a person used by others, not a wedge, and both poles are South.
annotation.definitionFit: Fish and frogs spawn by releasing their eggs into the water.

entries.clue: Used in USA to stop one masseur? (6)

annotation.definition2: Used in USA to stop one

blocks.clueFragment: Used in USA to stop one
blocks.note: American slang for a condom, which stops one baby arriving; in Britain the same word means an eraser.
A masseur is literally one who rubs.

annotation.surface: A question about what Americans use to halt a masseur.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a rubber rubs out pencil. The American sense is the one that stops one arriving, and the question mark flags a masseur as 'one who rubs'.
annotation.definitionFit: Rubber is US slang for a condom, and a masseur, who rubs clients, is literally a rubber.

entries.clue: Clare on the descent, which doesn't come up to requirements? (9)

annotation.definition: which doesn't come up to requirements?
annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a relative clause standing for a noun: the thing that fails to meet requirements.

blocks.note: Clare Short was a Labour cabinet minister who resigned over the Iraq war.
A descent is a fall.

annotation.surface: A politician on the way down fails to meet the standard.
annotation.walkthrough: Clare Short, the outspoken Labour minister, gives her surname. 'Come up to' sets up the joke on falling.
annotation.definitionFit: A shortfall is the amount by which something falls short of what is needed.

entries.clue: To depose Syria's leader declare "you're gay" all around (4)

indicatorNotes.leader: A word's leader is its first letter.
indicatorNotes.all around: All around means surrounding the other piece.

blocks.note: To out someone is to declare publicly that they are gay.
The first letter of 'Syria'.

annotation.surface: A scheme to topple President Assad of Syria by spreading rumours about his sexuality.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Syria's leader' suggests Assad, but here it is just the first letter of 'Syria'.
annotation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to force them from office, which is what deposing a ruler means.

entries.clue: Cluster buttock with extremes of temperature (5)

blocks.note: Buns is slang for buttocks.
Cold and hot, the two extremes, are C and H as marked on taps.

annotation.surface: A cluster of buttocks that runs hot and cold.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremes' usually means the first and last letters, which would give TE. Here it means the extremes of heat, cold and hot, marked C and H on a tap.
annotation.definitionFit: Grapes or flowers growing or gathered together in one cluster make a bunch.

entries.clue: Reject tot of Charles's ex? (8)

indicatorNotes.of: 'Tot of the ex' is the ex's tot, so the ex comes first.

blocks.note: Prince Charles's ex-wife was Diana, known as Di, so Charles's ex's is DI'S.
To tot up is to count.

annotation.surface: A question about disowning the child of Prince Charles's former wife.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a toddler, one of Diana's sons, but it is the verb from 'tot up'.
annotation.definitionFit: To discount an idea is to dismiss or reject it as not worth considering.

entries.clue: Over Ed Miliband's head, negative Scottish backing – "Humble" (6)

indicatorNotes.Over: Turned over, a word reads the other way round.
indicatorNotes.head: A word's head is its first letter.
indicatorNotes.backing: Backing means going backwards, so the letters are reversed.

blocks.note: ED turned over.
The first letter of 'Miliband'.
NAE is Scots for no, reversed by the backing.

annotation.surface: Scottish voters go over Ed Miliband's head and refuse to back him, which is humbling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over Ed Miliband's head' reads as bypassing the Labour leader. Here 'Over' reverses Ed and 'head' takes only Miliband's first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to humble or lower them in dignity.
